verses.1: And Elisha said, “Hear the words of the LORD.” Thus said the LORD: “From now on, there will be a day when heavy burdens and oppressive tasks will be carried by people. They will have to carry those burdens through the gate of Shemeron.”
verses.2: And the third one, who was the king’s servant, took hold of the man of God by his hand. He said, “Look! The LORD is doing this in the heavens. This will happen.” But the man of God replied, “I see with my eyes, but I will not eat from it.”
verses.3: And four men were standing at the door. They said to each other, “What are we doing here? We should have died by now.”
verses.4: If we say that we will enter the city and die there from hunger, then we have given up. But if we stay here and die instead, then go ahead and fall into Arma’s camp. If we survive, we will live; but if we die, then we have given up.
verses.5: And they stood at the entrance to Arma’s camp. They walked all the way to the edge of Arma’s camp. But there was no one there at all.
verses.6: And Adonai spoke out: “The army of Aram will sound the trumpet. It will be like the sound of horses, or the sound of a large army. They said to each other, ‘Look! The king of Israel has given us the kings of Hittite and the kings of Egypt as prisoners.’”
verses.7: And they got up and left their tents, as well as their animals and their livestock, which were kept in those shelters. They went away to their own homes.
verses.8: And these sick people came to the edge of the camp. They went into one of the tents, ate and drank there. They took away gold, silver, and other valuable items from there. Then they left and went to another tent. They also took away things from there.
verses.9: And they said to each other, “No, it isn’t so. We are doing this today, on this day of judgment. We will wait until tomorrow, and then we will go up to the king’s house and speak to him.”
verses.10: They came and called at the gate of the city. They were told, “We have come to the camp of Aram. But there is no one there. All that can be heard are the sounds of horses and chariots. There are no houses anywhere.”
verses.11: And the doors were called out, and the king’s house said, “Inside.”
verses.12: And the king got up at night and said to his servants, “Tell us what they have done to us.” They knew that we were hungry. So they left the camp and went into the field. They said, “Let’s go out of the city and take them alive.” Then they entered the city.
verses.13: And one of his servants said, “Please take five of the horses that remain in there. They are all from Israel. They are all those who remained in there after the others died.”
verses.14: They took two teams of horses, and the king sent them after the camp of Aram, saying, “Go and see.”
verses.15: And they went after them until they reached the Jordan. There, all the path was covered with clothes and utensils that people had thrown away in a hurry. Then the magicians returned and reported to the king.
verses.16: And the people went out and destroyed the camp of Aram. There were also many people who were killed in battle, just as Jehovah had commanded.
verses.17: And the king placed the third one, which was placed on his hand, at the door. The people carried it through the door. It died as soon as someone from God spoke to him.
verses.18: And when the man of God spoke to the king, he said, “Your gates will be filled with weights and measures. And tomorrow, at the gate of Zion, they will be filled even more.”
verses.19: And the third one tempted the man of God. He said, “Look! The LORD is making clouds rise from heaven. This will be a sign for you.” But the man of God replied, “You see with your own eyes, but you won’t be able to eat from it.”
verses.20: And so it happened that the people rushed at him through the door, and he died.
